title: Working preview (Gate 2): run the product, capture it, approve it in the browser
description:
Filed by architect-16a01670 from parent task-e7a3d643bde34da7b27495dbda745739 (epic breakdown, human-directed 2026-09-04).

PRODUCT GAP (README + VISION journey step 9 / Gate 2 'Approve Working Preview', re-measured 2026-09-04): 'there is no working preview'. `apps/daemon/src/graph-preview-request.ts` and `apps/control-room/src/preview/` are plan/document previews, not the product. The human-only decision pattern exists (`approval.decide`, `escalation.decide` in daemon-command-vocabulary.ts; HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS in daemon-command-families.ts; offers in http/affordance-read.ts; Needs-you cards in apps/control-room/src/v2/approvals/needs-you.tsx + offer-wire.ts). Process spawning with durable receipts exists (orchestrator/verifier-process-runner.ts, node-verifier.ts, node-lander.ts `moe-landing-receipt/1`). Playwright is installed (tests/e2e/control-room/playwright.config.ts).

FEATURE: a goal whose nodes are all landed (or the human's 'Start preview' click) gets a PREVIEW step. The daemon starts the product's preview command in the project workspace - from the approved contract's deployment requirements, default = the workspace package.json `preview` -> `dev` -> `start` script; port from the contract or detected from stdout - waits for the port, drives headless Chromium to the contract's journey entry URLs and captures one screenshot per journey (PNG under `<project>/.moe-next/previews/<goalId>/<sha>/`), records `moe-preview-receipt/1` {goalId, sha, url, pid, screenshots[], STARTED|REFUSED(code)}, then offers `preview.decide` (human-only, Gate 2: 'Is this product good enough and visually correct?') with APPROVE | REJECT{findings}. REJECT reopens the named nodes for rework carrying the findings (the review loop's REWORK column). The preview process is stopped on decision, on a 30-min timeout, and on daemon shutdown - no leaked process.

UI: Needs-you card 'Approve working preview' with the loopback URL (new tab), the screenshots inline, Approve / Reject-with-findings; goal status strip stage PREVIEW; Runs shows the preview receipt per goal. Refusals verbatim: PREVIEW_COMMAND_MISSING, PREVIEW_START_TIMEOUT, PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED, PREVIEW_DECISION_INVALID.

NOT in scope: deployment to an environment (row 'Containerized deployment'); the preview runs on the operator's machine.
definitionOfDone: `preview.decide` (and `preview.start` if the architect keeps a separate trigger) published human-only, MCP-excluded, in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS, with the full roster backfill and bidirectional roster tests; PREVIEW_COMMAND_MISSING, PREVIEW_START_TIMEOUT, PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED, PREVIEW_DECISION_INVALID each asserted with code + layer.

Preview runner test with a fixture product (a tiny http server as the `preview` script): the receipt has url + sha + at least one screenshot PNG whose bytes decode; the child pid is gone after APPROVE, after REJECT and after a forced timeout (assert process exit, not a flag).

Needs-you renders the card with link + screenshots + both buttons; APPROVE commits a durable decision read back from /activity/read (verdict); REJECT with findings moves the named node to REWORK on the board with the findings text visible.
Playwright journey under tests/e2e/control-room/ against a REAL daemon covers start -> card -> approve; `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted.
Live drive: a preview started for UnAI (or a fresh scaffold app) with a real screenshot (path + sha256) and the committed decision in a row comment; README 'no working preview' clause rewritten.
Gates quoted with their count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.

implementationPlan.note:
INTEGRATION-LEVEL ADVERSARIAL PASS across all four child diffs at once. Four questions, four answers, each measured. Full detail in a row comment; nothing filed as a new row (global rail 21).

(a) PROCESS LEAKS AFTER A CRASH — NOT COVERED, AND I FOUND ONE LIVE ON THIS MACHINE. The four cleanup arms are real (preview-supervisor.test.ts:130/144/158/202) and each asserts pid gone AND port free through the production `probeProcessAlive`. All four run through `close()`. A CRASH never calls `close()`, and there is NO boot-time reaper: `git grep -iE 'sweep|reap|stale' HEAD -- 'apps/daemon/src/preview/*.ts'` returns only shutdown-side comments. The receipt ledger is DURABLE while the supervisor roster is IN-MEMORY, so after a crash-restart the ledger still says STARTED while the roster is empty — and preview-supervisor.test.ts:239 pins that a decision naming no live preview "reports so rather than pretending it stopped one". Correct behaviour, but it means NOTHING reclaims the port; the operator must find the pid by hand. PROVEN, not theorised — a live orphan on this host right now: pid 62032 `npm run preview` (parent GONE, created 9/6 14:31, ~19h) -> pid 43024 `cmd.exe /d /s /c node server.mjs` -> pid 32188 LISTENING on 127.0.0.1:54392. Two more of the same family: pid 38760 (`node -e "const http=..."`, ~40h, holding 127.0.0.1:4178) and pid 70500 (UnAI live-drive lane.mjs, ~28h). CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER RECORD: task-4cbaca29's "leak census: NET ZERO" grepped command lines for `preview-server.js`. That string appears NOWHERE in the leaked tree — the runner spawns the workspace's `preview` SCRIPT, so the visible command is `npm run preview` and the server is a GRANDCHILD named whatever the workspace calls it. The census needle was too narrow; the conclusion it supported was wrong. Memory `gotcha-a-leaked-preview-hides-as-npm-run-preview-not-preview-server-js`.

(b) CONCURRENCY — SAFE ON PATHS AND BROWSER, AND ONE MISLEADING CODE ON PORTS. PATHS: the capture directory is `.moe-next/previews/<goalId>/<sha>` (preview-receipt-contracts.ts:84), so two goals cannot share a directory, and two starts of the SAME revision are serialised on the deterministic receipt id — asserted at preview-supervisor.test.ts:244 "two CONCURRENT starts of the same revision spawn ONE server, not two". BROWSER: `capturePreviewJourneys` launches its own Chromium and closes it in a `finally` (preview-capture.ts), so there is no shared instance to collide on — though a daemon crash MID-capture leaks that Chromium too, and it is not in the supervisor's roster. PORTS: `startPreviewProcess` pre-flights at preview-process.ts:200 — `if (input.port !== null && await portAccepts(input.port)) return previewRefusal("PREVIEW_START_TIMEOUT")`. That is the right REFUSAL with the WRONG WORD: nothing timed out, the port was taken before the spawn, and the operator-facing text (activity-words.ts:108) says "The product did not answer before the daemon stopped waiting", which tells them to retry when the fix is to free the port — plausibly the 19h orphan above. There is no PREVIEW_PORT_IN_USE code. Recorded, not fixed: adding a fifth code is a roster job across the four digest mirrors (epic rail 1) and epic rail 3 forbids moving those literals from a row that does not own them.

(c) TRUST / CAPTURE PATH — CANNOT ESCAPE.
